UKIEPC2023 H.History inNumbers 题解

History inNumbers

题目大意：

已知一个数列aa,数列中连续相同的数会被自动合并成一个数，你需要实现以下两种操作：

  • 将某区间所有数加上dd
  • 查询一个区间[s,f][s, f],判断该区间内所有的局部极小值是否呈严格递增趋势

如果一个数列中的一个数比它两边的数都小，若在数列两端，那么只与相邻的一个元素比较，这个数为这个数列的局部极小值。

数据范围：

  • 数列长度：1≤n≤3*1051 \le n \le 3 * 10^5,−108≤ai≤108-10^8 \le a_i \le 10^8
  • 操作数：1≤m≤3*1051 \le m \le 3 * 10^5,|d|≤108|d| \le 10 ^8

显然又是一个令人愉快(bushi)的线段树的题

设计维护信息

我们要想办法设计出根据其能在合并时判断是否有极小值生成，并且确认该区间的极小值序列是否是有序的（题目要求的严格递增）信息。区间加法使用一个简单的懒标记即可。

从两个区间合并时入手：新的极小值可能会在两个区间的中间出现，所以一个区间的左端点和右端点有成为极小值的潜力。为了判断，不仅要维护区间左右端点的值，还要维护区间在对应端点处的变化趋势。

合并时还要维护合并之后的极小值序列是否是严格递增的，因此还要存储每个区间极小值序列的第一个和最后一个元素，合并时只要判断这些元素之间的大小关系即可

合并时先合并连续相等的元素，再派出区间的两端，只统计内部极小值

合并区间极小值信息

先从简单的入手，当合并时，我们需要多次合并两个区间的信息，并且维护其最小值序列是否严格递增，设相邻两个区间为x和y,若x和y均有序且x的最后一个极小值小于y的第一个极小值，那么合并后的极小值序列也是严格递增的

维护线段树Node合并时新产生的极小值

令lval和rval代表区间左端点和右端点的取值，lr分别代表从左到右第一次、最后一次非零值变化方向，1表示增长，0表示相等，-1表示下降，设相邻的两个区间为u和v,分三种情况讨论：

  • u.valr<v.vallu.val_r< v.val_l:左区间的右端点是新的极小值当且仅当左区间在右端点处是下降趋势，即u.r == -1
  • u.valr>v.vallu.val_r > v.val_l:右区间的左端点是新的极小值当且仅当右区间在左端点处是上升趋势,即v.l == 1
  • u.valr=v.vallu.val_r = v.val_l:中间的两个端点可以合并成一个极小值当且仅当u.r == -1 && v.l == 1

建立线段树 & push_up

与常规的建树方式相同，需要注意每个值的初始化

push_up函数其实就是调用merge_node来合并当前点的左儿子和右儿子

实现区间修改以及懒标记下传

不难注意到，区间加法不会改变区间内部的大小关系，所以对极小值序列只会统一加一个偏移量，依然有序。只有区间的两端可能会产生新的极小值，这和建树时的情况相似，在递归过程中只需每次都push_up父节点即可实现维护。

在懒标记下传以及区间修改和查询时都会对节点内部大量的信息作加法修改，因此可以写一个函数来简化：

需要继续递归访问儿子时，先下传懒标记

区间加法的实现就很简单了，完整覆盖时直接modify并返回即可

实现查询操作

查询操作与常规线段树一致，只需注意返回的类型是整个节点即可

边界条件

区间的两个端点也可能成为极小值，如果查询时包含端点，只需在端点一侧插入一个极大值INF即可。

entry.title: UKIEPC 2023 H. History in Numbers — Solution
entry.content:
UKIEPC 2023 H.History in Numbers — Solution

Read theoriginal Chinese version

History inNumbers

Problem summary:

Given a sequenceaa,treat consecutive equal values as a single value. We need to support thefollowing two operations:

  • Addddto every element in an interval.
  • Query an interval[s,f][s, f]and check whether its local minima are strictly increasing from left toright.

An element is a local minimum if it is smaller than both of itsneighbours. At either end of the sequence, we only compare it with itsone neighbour.

Constraints:

  • Sequence length:1≤n≤3*1051 \le n \le 3 * 10^5,−108≤ai≤108-10^8 \le a_i \le 10^8
  • Number of operations:1≤m≤3*1051 \le m \le 3 * 10^5,|d|≤108|d| \le 10 ^8

Obviously, another delightful segment tree problem. (Justkidding.)

Choosing what to maintain

We need to work out what information lets us detect new local minimaduring a merge and check whether the resulting sequence of local minimais ordered—strictly increasing, as the problem requires. A simple lazytag will take care of range addition.

Let’s start with merging two intervals. A new local minimum mayappear where they meet, so the left and right endpoints of an intervalare potential local minima. To decide whether they become local minima,we need to maintain both their values and the direction of change neareach endpoint.

We also need to know whether the merged sequence of local minima isstrictly increasing. So we store the first and last local minima of eachinterval as well. During a merge, we only need to compare the values atthe joins between these sequences.

Treat consecutive equal elements as one, then exclude the twoendpoints: we only store the internal local minima.

Merging the local-minimuminformation

Let’s start with the easy part. We will need to merge the informationfrom two intervals several times, while keeping track of whether thesequence of local minima is strictly increasing. Call the two adjacentintervals x and y. If both are ordered, andthe last local minimum of x is smaller than the first oneof y, then the merged sequence is strictly increasingtoo.

Handling new localminima when merging nodes

Let lval and rval be the values at the leftand right endpoints. Reading from left to right, l andr record the first and last non-zero directions of change:1 means increasing and -1 means decreasing. Ifthere is no change, the direction is 0.

For two adjacent intervals u and v, thereare three cases:

  • u.rval < v.lval: the right endpoint of the leftinterval becomes a new local minimum if and only if that interval isdecreasing near its right endpoint, i.e. u.r == -1.
  • u.rval > v.lval: the left endpoint of the rightinterval becomes a new local minimum if and only if that interval isincreasing near its left endpoint, i.e. v.l == 1.
  • u.rval == v.lval: the two endpoints in the middle canbe merged into one local minimum if and only ifu.r == -1 && v.l == 1.

Building the segment tree& push_up

The tree is built in the usual way. Just pay attention to how eachvalue is initialized.

The push_up function simply callsmerge_node to merge the current node’s left and rightchildren.

Range updates and lazypropagation

It is not hard to see that adding the same value to an interval doesnot change the relative order of its elements. The local minima allreceive the same offset, so whether their sequence is strictlyincreasing stays unchanged. New local minima may appear only at theboundaries of the updated interval. This is similar to building thetree: just call push_up on the parent as we return fromeach recursive call.

Lazy propagation, updates, and queries all involve adding values toseveral fields in a node, so we can write a helper function to make thissimpler:

Before going down to the children, push down the lazy tag.

Range addition is now straightforward. If the node’s interval isfully covered, just call modify and return.

Implementing queries

The query works just like a normal segment tree query. The only thingto note is that we return the whole node.

Boundary cases

The two endpoints of the queried interval may also be local minima.To include them, we can simply put a very large value INFjust outside each endpoint.

entry.title: Persistent Data Structure - Segment Tree
entry.content:
Persistent DataStructure - Segment Tree

A persistent data structure is a data structure that always preservesthe previous version of itself when it is modified. Such data structuresare effectively immutable, as their operations do not update thestructure in place, but instead always yield a new updatedstructure.

You should be familiar with basic segment trees before reading thispost.

Problem Statement

Persistent SegmentTree

You need to maintain an arrayaawith a length ofNN,supporting the following two operations:

  1. Modify the value at a certain position in some historicalversion
  2. Query the value at a certain position in some historicalversion

In addition, each operation creates a new version. The version numberis the index of the current operation, starting from 1, while version 0represents the initial state of the array.

For operation 2, the newly created version is completely identical tothe version being queried, with no modifications made. In other words,the version generated by a query operation is simply a copy of theversion that was queried.

Input Format

The first line contains two positive integersNNandMM,representing the length of the array and the number of operations,respectively.

The second line containsNNintegers, where theii-thinteger isaia_i.

The nextMMlines each contain either 3 or 4 integers, representing one of thefollowing two operations. Suppose the current operation is theii-thoperation:

  1. For operation 1, the format isv 1 p c, meaning that based on versionvv,setapa_ptocc.
  2. For operation 2, the format is v 2 p,meaning that we query the value ofapa_pin versionvv.Note that this operation also creates a new version that isidentical to versionvv.
  • 1≤N,M≤1061 \le N, M \le 10^6
  • 1≤p≤n1 \le p \le n
  • −109≤ai,c≤109-10^9 \le a_i, c \le 10^9

Copy the path

It is not hard to see that the limit is not the time complexity, butthe space complexity. If we build a separate segment tree for everyversion, we will definitely exceed the memory limit.

If we change the value of a leaf node, only the node on the path fromthe root to that leaf node would change, so that we only want to copythe path instead of creating a new tree. This is the idea behind apersistent segment tree.

You can find that a new root corresponds to a new version, anddifferent versions share some nodes. Because of that, we cannot use(idx * 2) and (idx * 2 + 1) to calculate theleft son and right son.

Build The Tree

Use the Structure to maintain node information:

The build function is similar to an ordinary segment tree. The onlydifference is that each node is assigned a unique index using++cnt.

Here, rt is a reference to the nodeindex, so its type should be int &.

After calling build(t[rt].ls, ...), the newly allocatednode index will be written directly into the parent node’sls field.

Update the Tree

Let update(idx, l, r, q, val) denote the followingoperation: based on the interval[l,r][l,r]represented by the old node idx, update the value atposition q to val, and return the index of theroot node of the modified subtree.

At each level of recursion, we first execute:

This only copies the three integers stored in the current node. Itdoes not recursively copy the entire subtree. At this point, the newnode and the old node temporarily point to the same left and rightchildren.

Next, we recurse only into the side that contains q -the target path that we want to copy, and connect the returned new childindex to current. The child index on the other side remainsunchanged, which allows the two versions to share unchangedsubtrees.

Throughout the recursion, we maintain the two invariants:

  • the old node is never modified
  • in the new subtree, only the value at position q ischanged.

At the leaf node, we directly assign the new value. As the recursionreturns, we reconnect the copied nodes along the path, eventuallyobtaining the root of the new version.

It’s not enough to copy only the leaf node, since the leaf’s parentmust point to the new leaf, and the parent’s parent must also point tothe new child. Therefore, the entire path from the leaf up to the rootmust be copied.

Query

Just head out from the root node, choose the left subtree or theright subtree according to the query position, and return the value whenyou reach the target leaf node.

Attention: a query also creates a new version. Since no valueschange, the new version can share the entire tree.

Space Complexity

The initial segment tree hasnnleaf nodes. Since every internal node has exactly two children, the treecontains a total of2n−12n-1nodes.

Suppose there areuuupdate operations. Each update copies at most⌈log⁡2n⌉+1\lceil \log_2 n\rceil+1nodes, including the root and the leaf. Therefore, an upper bound on thetotal number of nodes is

(2n−1)+u(⌈log⁡2n⌉+1). (2n-1)+u\bigl(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+1\bigr).

Forn,m≤106n,m\le 10^6,each update creates at most 21 new nodes, so the total number of nodesis less than2.3×1072.3\times10^7.In the implementation below, we reserve MAXN * 23 nodes forthe node pool.

The node indices, version indices, and point values in the range[−109,109][-10^9,10^9]all fit within a 32-bit int. In a typical environment wherean int takes 4 bytes and each node takes 12 bytes, the nodepool uses about 263 MiB. Together with the base androot arrays, the three arrays use about 271 MiB in total.Since there are no range-sum queries in this problem, there is no needto use long long for every field.

More precisely, the complexities are:

  • Building the initial tree:O(n)O(n).
  • Each update or query:O(1+log⁡n)O(1+\log n).
  • Total space:O(n+m+u(1+log⁡n))O\bigl(n+m+u(1+\log n)\bigr),where the root array itself takesO(m)O(m)space.

In most cases, we simply write the complexity of each operation asO(log⁡n)O(\log n),and the total space complexity asO(n+mlog⁡n)O(n+m\log n).

Whenn=1n=1,an update still copies one leaf node.

entry.title: Convex Hull Trick
entry.content:
Convex Hull Trick

The Convex Hull Trick can speed up a dynamic programming transitionby treating each previous state as a line. In this post, we will derivethis transformation for a partitioning problem and explain how amonotonic deque reduces the running time fromO(n2)O(n^2)toO(n)O(n).

Problem analysis

Starting with a quadratic DP

Consider HNOI2008 ToyPacking.

There arennitems arranged in a line. Theii-thitem has lengthcic_i,and we need to partition the items into contiguous groups. For a group[l,r][l,r],the cost is

(r−l+∑k=lrck−L)2,\left(r-l+\sum_{k=l}^{r}c_k-L\right)^2,

whereLLis a constant. The termr−lr-laccounts for the one-unit gap between each pair of adjacent items in thegroup. Our goal is to minimize the total cost of all groups.

The constraints are

1≤n≤5×104,1≤L,ci≤107.1\le n\le 5\times 10^4,\qquad 1\le L,c_i\le 10^7.

Letfif_idenote the minimum total cost of partitioning the firstiiitems. Define the prefix sums as

Si=∑k=1ick,S0=f0=0.S_i=\sum_{k=1}^{i}c_k,\qquad S_0=f_0=0.

If the final group contains itemsj+1j+1throughii,its total length isSi−Sj+i−j−1S_i-S_j+i-j-1.Considering every possible starting position of this final group givesthe recurrence

fi=min0≤j<i{fj+(i−(j+1)+Si−Sj−L)2}=min0≤j<i{fj+(Si−Sj+i−j−1−L)2}.\begin{aligned}f_i&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+\left(i-(j+1)+S_i-S_j-L\right)^2\right\}\\&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+\left(S_i-S_j+i-j-1-L\right)^2\right\}.\end{aligned}

This straightforward solution checks every previous state for eachii,resulting in anO(n2)O(n^2)algorithm.

Rewriting the transition

Expanding the square allows us to separate the terms that depend onlyoniifrom those involvingjj.

Letai=Si+ia_i=S_i+i.We can then write

Si−Sj+i−j−1−L=ai−aj−L−1.S_i-S_j+i-j-1-L=a_i-a_j-L-1.

Now letxi=ai−L−1x_i=a_i-L-1.The recurrence becomes

fi=min0≤j<i{fj+(xi−aj)2}=xi2+min0≤j<i{−2ajxi+fj+aj2}.\begin{aligned}f_i&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+(x_i-a_j)^2\right\}\\&=x_i^2+\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{-2a_jx_i+f_j+a_j^2\right\}.\end{aligned}

For a fixedii,the termxi2x_i^2is the same for every candidatejj,so it can be moved outside the minimum.

Interpreting each state as aline

For each previous statejj,define a line

ℓj(x)=kjx+bj,\ell_j(x)=k_jx+b_j,

where

kj=−2aj=−2(Sj+j),bj=fj+aj2=fj+(Sj+j)2.k_j=-2a_j=-2(S_j+j),\qquadb_j=f_j+a_j^2=f_j+(S_j+j)^2.

Computingfif_inow requires finding the minimum value among these lines atx=xix=x_i,then addingxi2x_i^2:

fi=xi2+min0≤j<iℓj(xi).f_i=x_i^2+\min_{0\le j<i}\ell_j(x_i).

Once we have computedfif_i,we can construct its line and make it available to subsequent states. Wequery before inserting the new line because only states withj<ij<iare valid candidates.

Maintaining the candidatelines

To speed up the transition, we discard lines that cannot improve theanswer to any future query. However, we cannot keep only the line thatis currently optimal: a different line may become optimal as the querycoordinate changes.

We will use a deque under two conditions:

  • Lines are inserted in strictly decreasing order of slope.
  • Query coordinates are nondecreasing.

The first condition lets us remove redundant lines from the back ofthe deque. The second lets us discard lines from the front as we answerqueries.

Adding a new line

Consider three linesPP,QQ,andRRwith strictly decreasing slopes:

kP>kQ>kR.k_P>k_Q>k_R.

Thexx-coordinateof the intersection ofPPandQQis

X(P,Q)=bQ−bPkP−kQ.X(P,Q)=\frac{b_Q-b_P}{k_P-k_Q}.

ForQQto be no higher than bothPPandRR,we need

X(P,Q)≤x≤X(Q,R).X(P,Q)\le x\le X(Q,R).

Therefore, if

X(P,Q)≥X(Q,R),X(P,Q)\ge X(Q,R),

thenQQis never strictly better than bothPPandRR.When the two intersection coordinates are equal, all three lines meet atthe same point, soQQcan still be removed without changing the minimum value.

When inserting a new lineRR,we apply this test to the last two lines in the deque andRR.If the middle line is redundant, we remove it from the back and repeatthe test. We then appendRR.

Answering queries

Suppose the first two lines in the deque arePPandQQ,withkP>kQk_P>k_Q.If, at the current query coordinatexx,

Q(x)≤P(x),Q(x)\le P(x),

thenQQremains no higher thanPPfor every later coordinate. To see why, letx′≥xx'\ge x.We have

Q(x′)−P(x′)=Q(x)−P(x)+(kQ−kP)(x′−x)≤0.Q(x')-P(x')=Q(x)-P(x)+(k_Q-k_P)(x'-x)\le 0.

We can therefore removePPfrom the front of the deque. We repeat this comparison until only oneline remains or the first line is better than the second at the currentcoordinate.

The insertion step keeps the intersection coordinates of consecutivelines in increasing order. This ensures that, once the front comparisonsstop, the first line gives the minimum value among all remainingcandidates.

Applying the optimization

Returning to our problem, we have

ai+1−ai=ci+1+1>0.a_{i+1}-a_i=c_{i+1}+1>0.

Thus,aia_iis strictly increasing. The inserted slopeskj=−2ajk_j=-2a_jare strictly decreasing, and the query coordinatesxi=ai−L−1x_i=a_i-L-1are strictly increasing. Both conditions required by the deque aresatisfied.

Each line is inserted once and removed at most once, from either end.Although a single operation may remove several lines, there are onlyO(n)O(n)removals over the entire algorithm. The total running time is thereforeO(n)O(n),withO(n)O(n)space in the worst case.

Understanding theimplementation

Matching the code to therecurrence

The implementation below uses an equivalent arrangement of the samerecurrence. It keeps the query coordinate ataia_iand includes the constantL+1L+1in each line instead.

Define

tj=aj+L+1.t_j=a_j+L+1.

Then

fi=min0≤j<i{fj+(ai−tj)2}=ai2+min0≤j<i{(−2tj)ai+fj+tj2}.\begin{aligned}f_i&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+(a_i-t_j)^2\right\}\\&=a_i^2+\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{(-2t_j)a_i+f_j+t_j^2\right\}.\end{aligned}

The code therefore uses the following quantities:

CodeMeaning
s[i]The prefix sumSiS_i.
f[i]The minimum costfif_i.
x = s[i] + iThe current query coordinateaia_i.
tThe valuetj=aj+L+1t_j=a_j+L+1for the state whose line is being constructed.
line.firThe slope−2tj-2t_j.
line.secThe interceptfj+tj2f_j+t_j^2.

Here, fir and sec are macros forfirst and second. The deque stores each lineas a pair containing its slope and intercept. Since addingL+1L+1preserves the order of theaja_jvalues, the slopes still decrease and the query coordinates stillincrease.

Initializing the deque

The initial candidate is statej=0j=0,wherea0=f0=0a_0=f_0=0.Therefore,t0=L+1t_0=L+1,and its line is

y=−2(L+1)x+(L+1)2.y=-2(L+1)x+(L+1)^2.

This explains the initialization t = L + 1 andq.push_back({-2 * t, t * t}). State00represents placing all of the firstiiitems into a single group. The global arrays are zero-initialized,providing s[0] = f[0] = 0.

Querying the minimum

The helper value(line, x) evaluates a line at thecurrent coordinate. In the first while loop, ifq[1] is no higher than q[0], the first linecan be removed permanently. The <= comparison alsohandles ties: the second line has a smaller slope and is at least asgood for every future query.

After this loop, q.front() gives the minimum line value,so the assignment f[i] = x*x + value(q.front(), x) computesthe current DP state.

Inserting the current state

After computing f[i], the code setst = x + L + 1. Since x = a_i, this is exactlyti=ai+L+1t_i=a_i+L+1.The new line R has slope−2ti-2t_iand interceptfi+ti2f_i+t_i^2.

The helper check(A, B, C) determines whether the middleline B is redundant. It tests

X(A,B)≥X(B,C).X(A,B)\ge X(B,C).

BecausekA>kB>kCk_A>k_B>k_C,both denominators in the intersection formulas are positive. We cantherefore compare the intersections by cross multiplication:

(bB−bA)(kB−kC)≥(kA−kB)(bC−bB).(b_B-b_A)(k_B-k_C)\ge(k_A-k_B)(b_C-b_B).

This is the expression used in check, avoiding divisionwhen comparing intersection coordinates. The second whileloop removes redundant lines from the back, andq.push_back(R) makes the new state available to futurequeries.

entry.title: 最大流最小割、König 与 Dilworth 背后的对偶
entry.content:
学最大流最小割的时候，我总觉得它和 König 定理、Dilworth定理有点像。一个在讲流量，一个在讲匹配，还有一个在讲偏序集，最后却都得到一个“最大值等于最小值”。

因为它们都属于组合优化中的 min-max定理，然后就可以解释的通了

定理最大化什么最小化什么
最大流最小割源汇流量分开源汇的割容量
König，二分图匹配的边数点覆盖的点数
Dilworth，有限偏序集反链的元素数划分全部元素所需的链数

先看比较容易证明的一边

任意流量都不会超过任意割的容量。把源点和汇点分开以后，流量总得跨过去，割上的容量限制了它能过去多少。

匹配和点覆盖也有类似的关系。点覆盖要求每条边至少有一个端点被选中；匹配中的边互不共享端点，要覆盖这几条边，至少得分别选一个点。因此，对任意匹配MM和任意点覆盖CC，都有

|M|≤|C|.|M|\le |C|.

在偏序集中，链里的元素两两可比，反链里的元素两两不可比。一条链最多装下一个反链元素。若已经把全部元素划成kk条链，任何反链的大小都不超过kk。

这些不等式都有同一种用法。找到一个大小为55的匹配，只能说明答案至少是55；再找到一个大小为55的点覆盖，就能立刻确定答案。

这就是对偶最直观的作用。一边给出可行方案，另一边给出它无法继续改进的证明。困难的部分在于，两边能否总是找到数值相同的解。

最大流结束后，最小割已经在残量图里了

沿用最大流初步里的记号。没有增广路时，从ss出发，只沿正残余容量的边搜索，把能到达的点记为SS，其余点记为TT。

此时t∈Tt\in T。原图中从SS指向TT的边一定全部满流，否则还能走过去。原图中从TT指向SS的边则一定没有流量，否则它的残量反边也会让我们从SS走到TT。

把SS内所有点的流量守恒式相加，内部边互相抵消，留下

|f|=f(S,T)−f(T,S)=c(S,T).|f|=f(S,T)-f(T,S)=c(S,T).

我们得到了一个流和一个割，而且数值相同。结合任意流不超过任意割，两者同时最优。

这里没有要求容量是整数。整数容量带来的是另一个性质，存在整数最大流，这会在把流量解释成匹配时用到。

König定理可以直接从最小割得到

设二分图左右两部为L,RL,R，建立下面的网络。

连边容量
s→us o u，u∈Lu\in L11
u→vu o v，原图中有边(u,v)(u,v)INFINF
v→tv o t，v∈Rv\in R11

与二分图匹配里的建图相比，中间的容量改成了INFINF。左右两端仍然限制每个点最多通过一单位流量，整数最大流仍然对应最大匹配。

取INF=|L|+|R|+1INF=|L|+|R|+1就够了。只切掉源点的出边，代价已经不超过|L||L|，最小割不会选择切中间的INFINF边。

设最小割的源侧为SS，选择

C=(L\S)∪(R∩S).C=(L\setminus S)\cup(R\cap S).

也就是选左边到不了的点，以及右边能到达的点。

如果原图的一条边(u,v)(u,v)两端都没被选中，那么u∈Su\in S、v∉Sv otin S，它就跨过了割，贡献一个INFINF，与前面的判断矛盾。因此CC覆盖了所有边。

割掉的单位容量边恰好对应这些选中的点，于是

|C|=最小割=最大流=|M|.|C|= ext{最小割}= ext{最大流}=|M|.

任意点覆盖又都至少有|M||M|个点，König 定理就得到了。反过来，给定点覆盖CC，取S={s}∪(L\C)∪(R∩C)S=\{s\}\cup(L\setminus C)\cup(R\cap C)，也能构造一个容量为|C||C|的割。

沿用前面的 e + id邻接表，在上述网络上跑完最大流之后，可以直接恢复这个点覆盖。左部编号为1..nL，右部编号为 nL+1..nL+nR。

Dilworth又能接到二分图匹配上

设有限偏序集有nn个元素。把每个元素xx复制成左右两个点xL,xRx_L,x_R，当且仅当x<yx<y时连边xL→yRx_L o y_R。这里用严格关系，不连xL→xRx_L o x_R。

一条匹配边xL→yRx_L o y_R表示把yy接到xx后面。匹配保证每个元素至多有一个前驱、一个后继，严格偏序又保证不会成环。于是，大小为mm的匹配能把nn个元素接成n−mn-m条链。

反过来，如果已经划成kk条链，把每条链里相邻的元素连接起来，会得到n−kn-k条匹配边。因此，设最大匹配大小为mm，有

最少链划分数=n−m. ext{最少链划分数}=n-m.

还差一个同样大的反链。

由 König 定理，复制出来的二分图存在大小为mm的点覆盖CC。保留那些左右副本都不在CC中的原元素，组成集合

A={x∣xL∉C,xR∉C}.A=\{x\mid x_L otin C,\ x_R otin C\}.

若AA中存在x<yx<y，边xL→yRx_L o y_R的两个端点就都没有被覆盖。因此AA一定是反链。

CC只有mm个副本，至多排除mm个原元素，所以|A|≥n−m|A|\ge n-m。前面又已经构造出n−mn-m条链，每条链最多容纳一个反链元素，得到|A|≤n−m|A|\le n-m。两边合起来就是

最大反链大小=最少链划分数=n−m. oxed{ ext{最大反链大小}= ext{最少链划分数}=n-m}.

例如a<b<da<b<d、a<c<da<c<d，且b,cb,c不可比。匹配aLbR,bLdRa_Lb_R,b_Ld_R给出两条链(a,b,d)(a,b,d)和(c)(c)；点覆盖{aL,dR}\{a_L,d_R\}则留下反链{b,c}\{b,c\}。链数和反链大小都是22。

这里建图需要全部可比关系。 如果偏序关系来自 DAG中的可达性，就要考虑传递闭包。比如原图只有

a→c,b→c,c→d,c→e.a o c,\quad b o c,\quad c o d,\quad c o e.

只用这些原边建二分图，最大匹配为22，得到的最少点不相交路径覆盖为5−2=35-2=3。按可达关系建图后，还可以用b<db<d，把元素划为(a,c,e)(a,c,e)和(b,d)(b,d)两条链。链允许跳过中间元素，点不相交路径覆盖要求沿原边实际经过它们，这两种建图回答的问题不同。

线性规划把这种联系写成了公式

先把匹配写成一个优化问题。每条边设置变量xex_e，选这条边时取11，否则取00。每个点至多属于一条匹配边，因此有

max⁡∑e∈Exe,∑e∋vxe≤1(∀v),xe∈{0,1}.\max\sum_{e\in E}x_e,\qquad\sum_{e i v}x_e\le 1\quad( orall v),\qquad x_e\in\{0,1\}.

把最后一个条件放宽为xe≥0x_e\ge 0，就得到线性规划松弛。每条边关联的端点约束已经保证xe≤1x_e\le1。它的对偶为

min⁡∑v∈Vyv,yu+yv≥1(∀uv∈E),yv≥0.\min\sum_{v\in V}y_v,\qquady_u+y_v\ge 1\quad( orall uv\in E),\qquad y_v\ge 0.

如果yvy_v取00或11，它正好表示是否选择点vv；约束要求每条边至少有一个端点被选中。这就是点覆盖。

两个式子为什么互相限制，也可以直接算出来。

∑uv∈Exuv≤∑uv∈Exuv(yu+yv)=∑v∈Vyv∑e∋vxe≤∑v∈Vyv.\sum_{uv\in E}x_{uv}\le\sum_{uv\in E}x_{uv}(y_u+y_v)=\sum_{v\in V}y_v\sum_{e i v}x_e\le\sum_{v\in V}y_v.

这叫弱对偶。强对偶进一步保证，这对线性规划的最优值相等。

但它们现在允许分数。要回到真正的匹配和点覆盖，还需要说明分数不会把最优值改掉。二分图恰好具有这种整数性，可以从它的点边关联矩阵的全幺模性推出。这个性质要求每个方形子矩阵的行列式都在{−1,0,1}\{-1,0,1\}中；配合这里的整数约束，两个问题都存在整数最优解，点覆盖的整数变量也可截到00或11。

一般图就未必如此。拿三角形试一下。

问题要求选或不选允许分数
最大匹配11每条边取1/21/2，最优值3/23/2
最小点覆盖22每个点取1/21/2，最优值3/23/2

两个线性规划仍然满足强对偶，实际匹配与点覆盖的数值却不同。König定理里的“二分图”条件，就在这里起了作用。

最大流最小割也能沿着线性规划对偶来证明。严格地说，写出的对偶先含有实数点势变量，还要证明能从最优对偶解中取出同值的割。这样才把线性规划里的最优值，与图上能实际找出的割对应起来。

参考

  • MIT网络流与匹配讲义
  • MIT二分图匹配讲义
  • Princeton对偶与全幺模讲义
  • Hamburg离散数学讲义，第 40 页
  • IterativeMethods in Combinatorial Optimization，第 3 章

entry.title: The Duality Behind Max-Flow Min-Cut, König and Dilworth
entry.content:
Read the original Chineseversion

When I was learning the max-flow min-cut theorem, I kept feeling thatit was a bit like König’s theorem and Dilworth’s theorem. One is aboutflow, one is about matching, and the other is about partially orderedsets. Yet they all end up with “a maximum equals a minimum”.

They are all min-max theorems in combinatorialoptimisation, which makes the connection easier to understand.

TheoremWhat do we maximise?What do we minimise?
Max-flow min-cutFlow from the source to the sinkCapacity of a cut separating the source and sink
König, for bipartite graphsNumber of edges in a matchingNumber of vertices in a vertex cover
Dilworth, for finite partially ordered setsNumber of elements in an antichainNumber of chains needed to partition all elements

Start with the easier sideto prove

The value of any flow cannot exceed the capacity of any cut. Once weseparate the source and sink, the flow has to cross the cut, and thecapacity of the cut limits how much can get through.

Matching and vertex cover have a similar relationship. A vertex coverrequires at least one endpoint of every edge to be selected. The edgesin a matching share no endpoints, so covering these edges requires us toselect at least one vertex for each of them. Therefore, for any matchingMMand any vertex coverCC,we have

|M|≤|C|.|M|\le |C|.

In a partially ordered set, every pair of elements in achain is comparable, while every pair of distinctelements in an antichain is incomparable. A chain cancontain at most one element of an antichain. If we have partitioned allelements intokkchains, any antichain has size at mostkk.

These inequalities all serve the same purpose. Finding a matching ofsize55only tells us that the answer is at least55.If we also find a vertex cover of size55,we immediately know the answer.

This is the most intuitive use of duality. One side gives usa feasible solution, and the other proves that it cannot be improved anyfurther. The difficult part is whether we can always findsolutions with the same value on both sides.

Oncemax flow finishes, the min cut is already in the residual graph

We will use the notation from Network Flow Basics. Whenthere is no augmenting path, start a search fromss,following only edges with positive residual capacity. Call the set ofreachable verticesSS,and put the remaining vertices inTT.

At this point,t∈Tt\in T.Every edge fromSStoTTin the original graph must be full; otherwise, we could still cross it.Every edge fromTTtoSSin the original graph must carry no flow; otherwise, its reverse edge inthe residual graph would also let us move fromSStoTT.

Adding up the flow conservation equations for the vertices inSS,the internal edges cancel out, leaving

|f|=f(S,T)−f(T,S)=c(S,T).|f|=f(S,T)-f(T,S)=c(S,T).

We have found a flow and a cut with the same value. Since any flow isbounded by any cut, both must be optimal.

There is no requirement here for capacities to be integers. Integercapacities give us a separate property: an integer maximum flowexists. We will need this when interpreting flow as amatching.

König’s theoremfollows directly from min cut

Let the two sides of a bipartite graph beL,RL,R.Build the following network.

EdgeCapacity
s→us\to u,whereu∈Lu\in L11
u→vu\to v,where(u,v)(u,v)is an edge in the original graphINFINF
v→tv\to t,wherev∈Rv\in R11

Compared with the construction in Bipartite Matching, thecapacities of the middle edges have changed toINFINF.The edges at both ends still limit each vertex to at most one unit offlow, so an integer maximum flow still corresponds to a maximummatching.

TakingINF=|L|+|R|+1INF=|L|+|R|+1is enough. Cutting only the outgoing edges of the source already costsat most|L||L|,so a minimum cut will never choose to cut a middle edge with capacityINFINF.

LetSSbe the source side of a minimum cut, and choose

C=(L\S)∪(R∩S).C=(L\setminus S)\cup(R\cap S).

In other words, choose the unreachable vertices on the left and thereachable vertices on the right.

If neither endpoint of an original edge(u,v)(u,v)were selected, thenu∈Su\in Sandv∉Sv\notin S.This edge would cross the cut and contributeINFINF,contradicting what we just showed. Therefore,CCcovers every edge.

The unit-capacity edges crossing the cut correspond exactly to theselected vertices, so

|C|=min cut=max flow=|M|.|C|=\text{min cut}=\text{max flow}=|M|.

Every vertex cover also has at least|M||M|vertices, which proves König’s theorem. Conversely, given a vertex coverCC,we can takeS={s}∪(L\C)∪(R∩C)S=\{s\}\cup(L\setminus C)\cup(R\cap C)to construct a cut of capacity|C||C|.

Using the same e + id adjacency list as before, we canrecover this vertex cover directly after running max flow on thenetwork above. The left vertices are numbered1..nL, and the right vertices are numberednL+1..nL+nR.

Dilworth connectsto bipartite matching too

Suppose a finite partially ordered set hasnnelements. Make a left and a right copy of each elementxx,calledxL,xRx_L,x_R.Add an edgexL→yRx_L\to y_Rif and only ifx<yx<y.We use the strict relation here, so there is no edgexL→xRx_L\to x_R.

A matching edgexL→yRx_L\to y_Rmeans placingyydirectly afterxx.The matching ensures that each element has at most one predecessor andone successor, while the strict partial order prevents cycles.Therefore, a matching of sizemmconnects thennelements inton−mn-mchains.

Conversely, if we have a partition intokkchains, connecting consecutive elements in each chain gives usn−kn-kmatching edges. So, if the maximum matching has sizemm,then

minimum chain partition size=n−m.\text{minimum chain partition size}=n-m.

We still need an antichain of the same size.

By König’s theorem, the bipartite graph of copies has a vertex coverCCof sizemm.Keep the original elements whose left and right copies are both outsideCC,giving the set

A={x∣xL∉C,xR∉C}.A=\{x\mid x_L\notin C,\ x_R\notin C\}.

If there were elementsx<yx<yinAA,neither endpoint of the edgexL→yRx_L\to y_Rwould be covered. Therefore,AAmust be an antichain.

CCcontains onlymmcopies, so it excludes at mostmmoriginal elements. This gives|A|≥n−m|A|\ge n-m.We have also already constructedn−mn-mchains, and each chain can contain at most one antichain element, so|A|≤n−m|A|\le n-m.Putting the two sides together gives

maximum antichain size=minimum chain partition size=n−m.\boxed{\begin{gathered}\text{maximum antichain size}\\=\text{minimum chain partition size}\\=n-m\end{gathered}}.

For example, supposea<b<da<b<danda<c<da<c<d,whileb,cb,care incomparable. The matchingaLbR,bLdRa_Lb_R,b_Ld_Rgives two chains,(a,b,d)(a,b,d)and(c)(c).The vertex cover{aL,dR}\{a_L,d_R\}leaves the antichain{b,c}\{b,c\}.Both the number of chains and the antichain size are22.

This construction needs all comparable pairs. If thepartial order comes from reachability in a DAG, we need to consider thetransitive closure. For example, suppose the original graph only has

a→c,b→c,c→d,c→e.a\to c,\quad b\to c,\quad c\to d,\quad c\to e.

If we build the bipartite graph using only these original edges, themaximum matching has size22,giving a minimum vertex-disjoint path cover of size5−2=35-2=3.If we use reachability instead, we can also useb<db<dand partition the elements into two chains,(a,c,e)(a,c,e)and(b,d)(b,d).Chains can skip intermediate elements, while vertex-disjoint paths mustactually pass through them along the original edges. These twoconstructions answer different questions.

Linearprogramming writes this connection as formulas

First, write matching as an optimisation problem. Give each edge avariablexex_e,which is11if we select the edge and00otherwise. Each vertex can belong to at most one matching edge, so wehave

max⁡∑e∈Exe,∑e∋vxe≤1(∀v),xe∈{0,1}.\max\sum_{e\in E}x_e,\qquad\sum_{e\ni v}x_e\le 1\quad(\forall v),\qquad x_e\in\{0,1\}.

Relaxing the last condition toxe≥0x_e\ge 0gives a linear programming relaxation. The constraints at the endpointsof each edge already ensurexe≤1x_e\le1.Its dual is

min⁡∑v∈Vyv,yu+yv≥1(∀uv∈E),yv≥0.\min\sum_{v\in V}y_v,\qquady_u+y_v\ge 1\quad(\forall uv\in E),\qquad y_v\ge 0.

Ifyvy_vis00or11,it tells us exactly whether vertexvvis selected. The constraints require at least one endpoint of every edgeto be selected. This is vertex cover.

We can also calculate directly why the two expressions bound eachother.

∑uv∈Exuv≤∑uv∈Exuv(yu+yv)=∑v∈Vyv∑e∋vxe≤∑v∈Vyv.\sum_{uv\in E}x_{uv}\le\sum_{uv\in E}x_{uv}(y_u+y_v)=\sum_{v\in V}y_v\sum_{e\ni v}x_e\le\sum_{v\in V}y_v.

This is called weak duality. Strongduality goes further and guarantees that the optimal values ofthese two linear programs are equal.

But they now allow fractions. To get back to actual matchings andvertex covers, we still need to show that allowing fractions does notchange the optimal values. Bipartite graphs have exactly thisintegrality property, which follows from the totalunimodularity of their vertex-edge incidence matrices. Thisproperty requires every square submatrix to have a determinant in{−1,0,1}\{-1,0,1\}.Together with the integer right-hand sides here, it means both problemshave integer optimal solutions. The integer variables for vertex covercan also be capped so that they only take values of00or11.

This does not necessarily hold for general graphs. Try atriangle.

ProblemSelect it or leave it outFractions allowed
Maximum matching11Assign1/21/2to every edge; the optimum is3/23/2
Minimum vertex cover22Assign1/21/2to every vertex; the optimum is3/23/2

The two linear programs still satisfy strong duality, but the actualmatching and vertex cover have different values. This is where the“bipartite graph” condition in König’s theorem matters.

Max-flow min-cut can also be proved through linear programmingduality. Strictly speaking, the dual we first write down containsreal-valued vertex potential variables. We still need to prove that wecan extract a cut with the same value from an optimal dual solution.Only then have we connected the optimal value in the linear program to acut we can actually find in the graph.

References

  • MITlecture notes on network flow and matching
  • MITlecture notes on bipartite matching
  • Princetonlecture notes on duality and total unimodularity
  • Hamburglecture notes on discrete mathematics, page 40
  • IterativeMethods in Combinatorial Optimization, Chapter 3

entry.title: 费用流 & 二分图带权匹配
entry.content:
上一篇把二分图匹配转成了最大流。一单位流量代表一对匹配，容量限制保证每个点最多被选一次。如果每对匹配还有不同的收益，选择哪些边也会影响答案。

费用流给每条边再加一个单位费用。增广和反向边的操作仍然保留，只是找路径时，多了一笔要算的账。

先把目标说清楚

最小费用最大流的优先级是流量最大，其次费用最小。假设两种方案的流量分别为33和44，即使后者贵一些，仍然选择流量为44的方案。

有些题目已经规定必须完成KK项任务，这时流量固定为KK，只比较费用。能送出的最大流不足KK就无解，不能拿当前费用当答案。

设原边ee的流量为fef_e，单位费用为wew_e，总费用为

∑e∈Efewe.\sum_{e\in E} f_e w_e.

这里的wew_e是每单位流量的费用。一次增广推了33单位，路径每单位费用为55，答案应该增加1515。

沿用之前的邻接表，只需给 Edge 加上w。c继续表示残余容量，不能因为多了一个费用就把两者混起来。

反向边也要退费

最大流中，走反向边可以撤销之前送出的流量。现在原边上每送一单位需要支付ww，撤销时就要退回ww，所以反向边的费用是−w-w。

反边仍然从容量 0开始，正向边流过多少，才允许撤销多少。若题目原图本来就有两个相反方向的边，需要分别add()，各自建立自己的残量反边。

这也让最短路变得稍微麻烦了一点。即使输入费用全部非负，增广之后仍然可能出现有正残量的负费用反边，直接把原费用丢给Dijkstra 就不行了。

从最短增广路入手

EK用 BFS找边数最少的增广路。费用流比较的是沿途费用之和，所以要在残量网络中找费用最小的源汇路径。

每找到一条路径，就取沿途残余容量的最小值作为增广量，再更新正反边。路径中可以有反向边，它们会把之前某些选择的费用抵消掉。

在初始残量网络没有负费用环的前提下，沿最短费用增广路推流，可以保持当前流量下的费用最优。一直推到无法到达汇点，就得到最小费用最大流。

固定流量下，两个可行方案的差可以在残量网络中分解成若干个环。如果存在费用更低的方案，其中至少有一个环的费用为负；反过来，沿负费用环调整流量，也能在流量不变时降低费用。最短路增广会保持残量网络中没有负费用环，这保证了每一步的最优性。后面的势能也能用来理解这个条件。

最直接的实现是每轮跑 SPFA，它能处理负费用边。SPFA 的最坏复杂度为O(VE)O(VE)，每次增广都来一遍，会把时间花在重复的最短路上。这里使用初始SPFA 加势能 Dijkstra，反向边仍然按原规则维护。

用势能调整边权

给每个点维护一个势能 h[u]，搜索时把边权改成

w′(u,v)=w(u,v)+h[u]−h[v].w'(u,v)=w(u,v)+h[u]-h[v].

先看这样改会不会把最短路改掉。一条从ss到tt的路径上，中间点的势能一加一减恰好抵消，最后只剩

∑w′=∑w+h[s]−h[t].\sum w' = \sum w+h[s]-h[t].

所有源汇路径都加上同一个数，费用大小关系不变。接下来只要让搜索涉及的w′w'非负，就可以用 Dijkstra。

第一次用 SPFA 求源点到各个可达点的最短距离，并令 h[v]等于这个距离。由最短路的三角不等式

h[v]≤h[u]+w(u,v),h[v]\le h[u]+w(u,v),

可以得到可达部分的正残量边满足w′(u,v)≥0w'(u,v)\ge0。如果一开始所有正残量边的费用都非负，直接令势能全为0 即可。

之后每轮 Dijkstra 得到调整费用下的距离dist，对所有可达点执行

新的调整费用为w′(u,v)+dist[u]−dist[v]w'(u,v)+dist[u]-dist[v]，仍然非负。最短路上的边在更新后调整费用为0，增广新产生的反边也为 0，下一轮还能继续用Dijkstra。

实现时有两个地方要分开看。dist[t]是调整后的费用，不能直接乘流量加进答案；下面沿 pre回溯，累加原始 w 得到path_cost。此外，既然后面要用所有可达点的距离更新势能，就让Dijkstra 完整跑完，不在弹出汇点时提前返回。

费用流模板

pre[v] 保存进入 v的边编号，重边也能准确更新。need表示本次最多增加多少流量，返回值是本次增加的流量与费用。

代码里的 only_negative用于后面的可选匹配问题，普通最小费用最大流保持默认false。

建图后调用 min_cost_flow()即可求最小费用最大流。若要求恰好KK单位，调用 min_cost_flow(K) 并检查返回的flow == K，要求K≥0K\ge0。

给二分图匹配加上权值

源点、左右两侧和汇点的编号沿用上一篇。假设配对(u,v)(u,v)的收益为 weight，只需把对应边的费用设为-weight。

连边容量费用
s -> u10
u -> nL+v1-weight
nL+v -> t10

一单位流量对应一对匹配，总收益为-cost。这张图的初始正残量边从源点经过左部、右部，再到汇点，没有有向环，也就没有负费用环。

源点到左部、右部到汇点的容量都是1，所以任何点都无法参与两对匹配。容量为整数，增广量也为整数，选中配对的净流量只能为0 或1。反过来，一组合法匹配可以沿对应的源汇路径各送一单位流量，两种方案一一对应。

到这里还不能急着跑满。题目究竟要最多的配对，还是最高的总收益，会影响停止条件。

考虑三条允许的配对，L1R1L_1R_1的收益为1010，L1R2L_1R_2和L2R1L_2R_1的收益各为44。

只选L1R1L_1R_1，总收益为1010。改成另外两对，匹配数增加到22，收益却降到88。所有边权都是正数，仍然会出现这种差别。

选中收益为1010的边以后，下一次增广会经过它的反向边。新增两条配对，撤销旧的一条，原始路径费用为

−4+10−4=2.-4+10-4=2.

这次增广让匹配数增加一，同时让收益减少二。算到这里，两种目标就很清楚了。

目标处理方法
只要求总收益最大，允许少选只有 path_cost < 0 才增广
先匹配最多，再让总收益最大一直增广到没有路径
恰好匹配KK对，收益最大最多增广到KK，最后检查是否达到

最短增广路的边际费用不会下降，因此可选匹配模式在最短路径费用非负时可以停止。它会跳过费用为0 的增广，所以不保证总收益相同时匹配数最多。

完整匹配用法

把下面的代码接在费用流核心后即可运行。MATCH_MODE 的1 / 2 / 3 分别对应上表三种目标。

前两种模式输入 nL nR m，模式 3 输入nL nR m K。接下来mm行为 u v weight，左右两侧各自从 1开始编号。首行输出匹配数和总收益，后面输出配对；固定KK不可行时输出 -1。

恢复方案仍然检查最终残量。候选边初始容量为1，对应反边容量为 1时，说明这对匹配最终被选中。中途增广过的边可能被撤销，不能看到一次流过就把它永久记进答案。

两侧各有nn个点，要求完美匹配时，选模式 3 并令K=n。如果输入的是需要支付的费用price，配对边直接使用 price，输出cost；再按题意选择数量优先或固定流量的调用方式。

复杂度和使用范围

设原边数为EE、点数为VV，成功增广AA次。需要 SPFA 时，初始化最坏为O(VE)O(VE)；不需要时只用O(V+E)O(V+E)。这份实现的优先队列允许重复入堆，每轮Dijkstra 为O(V+Elog⁡(E+2))O(V+E\log(E+2))，一共至多A+1A+1轮搜索，空间为O(V+E)O(V+E)。二分图匹配每次增加一对，因此A≤min⁡(nL,nR)A\le\min(n_L,n_R)。

模板要求容量为非负整数、源汇不同，并且初始残量网络没有负费用环。有负费用环的题目可能仍然有有限最优解，只是需要额外处理，本模板没有消环步骤。

容量和费用都用了 long long，还要保证pushed * path_cost等中间运算不溢出，有限距离及势能的绝对值小于 INF。多测先init_graph()；同一张图比较不同目标时，重新建图或恢复初始e。直接再次调用会沿用已经修改的残量容量，返回的也只是这一次增加的量。

参考 MIT6.854 的费用流讲义，其中给出了最短费用增广和势能的正确性说明。

entry.title: Min-Cost Flow & Weighted Bipartite Matching
entry.content:
Read the original Chineseversion

The previous post turnedbipartite matching into a maximum flow problem. One unit of flowrepresents one matched pair, and the capacity limits ensure that eachvertex is chosen at most once. If different pairs also give differentprofits, which edges we choose will affect the answer as well.

Min-cost flow gives each edge a cost per unit of flow. We stillaugment the flow and use reverse edges, but now there is a cost to keeptrack of when finding a path.

First, be clear about theobjective

Minimum-cost maximum flow means maximising the flow first,then minimising the cost. Suppose two solutions send flows of33and44.Even if the second one costs more, we still choose the solution with aflow of44.

Some problems already require us to complete exactlyKKtasks. In that case, the flow is fixed atKK,and we only compare costs. If the maximum possible flow is less thanKK,there is no solution. We cannot use the cost found so far as theanswer.

Let the flow on an original edgeeebefef_e,and letwew_ebe its cost per unit. The total cost is

∑e∈Efewe.\sum_{e\in E} f_e w_e.

Here,wew_eis the cost of each unit of flow. If one augmentation sends33units along a path with a cost of55per unit, the answer should increase by1515.

We can keep the adjacency list from before and just addw to Edge. c still represents theresidual capacity. Adding a cost does not mean we can mix the twoup.

Reverse edges need torefund the cost too

In maximum flow, following a reverse edge lets us undo flow that wesent earlier. Now, sending one unit along the original edge costsww,so undoing it should refundww.That is why the reverse edge has a cost of−w-w.

The reverse edge still starts with a capacity of 0. Wecan only undo as much flow as has passed through the forward edge. Ifthe input graph already contains two edges in opposite directions, calladd() separately for each one, giving each its own reverseedge in the residual network.

This also makes shortest paths a little more complicated. Even if allinput costs are non-negative, an augmentation can create reverse edgeswith positive residual capacity and negative costs. We cannot simplygive the original costs to Dijkstra.

Start with shortestaugmenting paths

EK uses BFS to findan augmenting path with the fewest edges. For min-cost flow, we comparethe sum of the costs along the path, so we need to find asource-to-sink path with the lowest cost in the residualnetwork.

Whenever we find a path, take the smallest residual capacity along itas the amount to send, then update the forward and reverse edges. Thepath may include reverse edges, which cancel the costs of some earlierchoices.

As long as the initial residual network has no negative-cost cycles,augmenting along a shortest-cost path keeps the cost optimal for thecurrent amount of flow. Continue until the sink is unreachable, and weget minimum-cost maximum flow.

For a fixed amount of flow, the difference between two feasiblesolutions can be split into cycles in the residual network. If a cheapersolution exists, at least one of these cycles has a negative cost.Conversely, adjusting the flow along a negative-cost cycle reduces thecost without changing the amount of flow. Shortest-path augmentationkeeps the residual network free of negative-cost cycles, whichguarantees optimality at each step. The potentials below give us anotherway to understand this condition.

The most direct implementation runs SPFA in every round, since it canhandle negative-cost edges. SPFA has a worst-case complexity ofO(VE)O(VE),and running it for every augmentation means spending a lot of timerepeating shortest-path searches. Here, we use an initial SPFA followedby Dijkstra with potentials. Reverse edges are maintained in exactly thesame way as before.

Adjust edge costs withpotentials

Maintain a potential h[u] for each vertex, and use thefollowing edge cost during the search:

w′(u,v)=w(u,v)+h[u]−h[v].w'(u,v)=w(u,v)+h[u]-h[v].

First, let us check whether this changes the shortest path. Along apath fromsstott,the potential of each intermediate vertex is added once and subtractedonce. They cancel out, leaving only

∑w′=∑w+h[s]−h[t].\sum w' = \sum w+h[s]-h[t].

Every source-to-sink path has the same value added to its cost, sotheir order by cost stays the same. Now, as long as thew′w'values used in the search are non-negative, we can use Dijkstra.

For the first round, use SPFA to find the shortest distance from thesource to each reachable vertex, and set h[v] to thatdistance. The triangle inequality for shortest paths gives

h[v]≤h[u]+w(u,v),h[v]\le h[u]+w(u,v),

so every edge with positive residual capacity in the reachable partsatisfiesw′(u,v)≥0w'(u,v)\ge0.If all edges with positive residual capacity have non-negative costs atthe start, we can simply set every potential to 0.

In each later round, Dijkstra gives us the distancesdist under the adjusted costs. For every reachable vertex,apply

The new adjusted cost isw′(u,v)+dist[u]−dist[v]w'(u,v)+dist[u]-dist[v],which is still non-negative. After this update, the adjusted cost ofevery edge on a shortest path is 0. The reverse edgescreated by augmentation also have an adjusted cost of 0, sowe can keep using Dijkstra in the next round.

There are two details to keep separate in the implementation.dist[t] is the adjusted cost, so we cannot multiply it bythe flow and add it directly to the answer. The code below followspre backwards and sums the original w valuesto get path_cost. Also, since we need the distances of allreachable vertices to update the potentials, let Dijkstra finish insteadof returning as soon as the sink is popped.

Min-cost flow template

pre[v] stores the index of the edge enteringv, so even parallel edges can be updated correctly.need is the maximum amount of flow to add in this call. Thereturned values are the flow and cost added by this call.

The only_negative option is for the optional matchingproblem later on. For ordinary minimum-cost maximum flow, leave it atthe default value, false.

After building the graph, call min_cost_flow() to findminimum-cost maximum flow. If you need exactlyKKunits, call min_cost_flow(K) and check that the returnedflow == K, withK≥0K\ge0.

Add weights to bipartitematching

Keep the numbering of the source, left and right vertices, and sinkfrom the previous post. If the pair(u,v)(u,v)gives a profit of weight, just set the cost of its edge to-weight.

EdgeCapacityCost
s -> u10
u -> nL+v1-weight
nL+v -> t10

One unit of flow represents one matched pair, and the total profit is-cost. Initially, the edges with positive residual capacitygo from the source to the left side, then to the right side, and finallyto the sink. There are no directed cycles, so there are no negative-costcycles either.

The edges from the source to the left side and from the right side tothe sink all have capacity 1, so no vertex can belong totwo matched pairs. The capacities are integers, so the amounts sentduring augmentation are integers too. The net flow on a candidate pairedge can only be 0 or 1. Conversely, any validmatching can send one unit of flow along the correspondingsource-to-sink path for each pair. The two kinds of solutions correspondone to one.

At this point, we should not rush to send as much flow as possible.Whether the problem wants the most pairs or the highest total profitchanges when we should stop.

Consider three allowed pairs:L1R1L_1R_1gives a profit of1010,whileL1R2L_1R_2andL2R1L_2R_1each give44.

Choosing onlyL1R1L_1R_1gives a total profit of1010.Switching to the other two pairs increases the matching size to22,but lowers the profit to88.This difference can appear even when all edge weights are positive.

After choosing the edge with profit1010,the next augmentation goes through its reverse edge. It adds two newpairs and removes the old one, with an original path cost of

−4+10−4=2.-4+10-4=2.

This augmentation increases the matching size by one while reducingthe profit by two. With this calculation, the two objectives becomeclear.

ObjectiveWhat to do
Maximise total profit; choosing fewer pairs is allowedAugment only when path_cost < 0
Maximise the number of pairs first, then total profitKeep augmenting until no path remains
Match exactlyKKpairs with the highest total profitAugment up toKK,then check whether it was reached

The marginal cost of shortest augmenting paths never decreases, sothe optional matching mode can stop when the shortest path has anon-negative cost. It skips augmentations with a cost of 0,so it does not guarantee the most pairs among matchings with the sametotal profit.

Complete matching example

Add the following code after the min-cost flow core to run it. Values1 / 2 / 3 of MATCH_MODE correspond to thethree objectives in the table above.

The first two modes read nL nR m, while mode3 reads nL nR m K. The nextmmlines contain u v weight, with each side numberedseparately from 1. The first output line gives the numberof pairs and the total profit, followed by the pairs themselves. Ifmatching exactlyKKpairs is impossible, the output is -1.

To recover the matching, we still check the final residualcapacities. Each candidate edge starts with capacity 1. Ifits reverse edge has capacity 1, that pair is selected inthe final matching. An edge used during an earlier augmentation maylater be undone, so we cannot permanently add it to the answer justbecause flow passed through it once.

If each side hasnnvertices and we need a perfect matching, choose mode 3 andset K=n. If the input gives a cost to pay,price, use price directly as the cost of thepair edge and output cost. Then choose either themaximum-flow or fixed-flow call according to the problem.

Complexity and when to useit

LetEEbe the number of original edges,VVthe number of vertices, andAAthe number of successful augmentations. When SPFA is needed,initialisation takesO(VE)O(VE)in the worst case; otherwise, it only takesO(V+E)O(V+E).This implementation allows duplicate entries in the priority queue, soeach Dijkstra run takesO(V+Elog⁡(E+2))O(V+E\log(E+2)).There are at mostA+1A+1searches in total, and the space complexity isO(V+E)O(V+E).In bipartite matching, each augmentation adds one pair, soA≤min⁡(nL,nR)A\le\min(n_L,n_R).

The template requires non-negative integer capacities, differentsource and sink vertices, and an initial residual network with nonegative-cost cycles. A problem with negative-cost cycles may still havea finite optimal solution, but it needs extra handling. This templatedoes not include cycle cancellation.

Both capacities and costs use long long, butintermediate calculations such as pushed * path_cost muststill fit within the type. The absolute values of finite distances andpotentials must also stay below INF. Callinit_graph() before each test case. When comparingdifferent objectives on the same graph, rebuild it or restore theinitial e. Calling the function again directly uses theresidual capacities already changed by the previous call, and returnsonly the flow and cost added in the new call.

See the MIT6.854 notes on min-cost flow for the correctness of shortest-costaugmentation and potentials.

entry.title: Dinic & 二分图最大匹配
entry.content:
在 EK 中，每次 BFS找到一条增广路，推完流量以后就重新搜索。问题是，这次 BFS已经找到了很多点的最短距离，最后只用上一条路径，多少有点可惜。

能不能保留这次搜索的结果，把同样长度的增广路多找几条，再重新BFS？Dinic 就沿着这个想法继续做。

先把残量网络分层

令 level[u] 表示从源点到 u最少经过几条残量边。BFS 仍然只走残余容量大于零的边，得到层数以后，DFS再加一个限制。

也就是每次只能往下一层走。由这些边组成的图称为层次图。

这样走到汇点时，经过的边数一定等于level[t]，正好是一条最短增广路。层数沿路径严格增加，DFS也不会在环里绕回来，不需要再维护普通 DFS 的 vis 数组。

这里的分层对象是当前残量网络。原边和反向边都参与BFS，只要有剩余容量就可以走。假如反向边在这一轮恰好从第kk层通向第k+1k+1层，它同样可以进入层次图。

一轮 BFS 能用多久

固定层数以后，反复从源点 DFS，每次找到一条路径就推送瓶颈流量，直到DFS 返回 0。

此时本轮层次图中的每条源汇路径都至少有一条边被用满，已经无法继续沿着层数递增的方向增广。这一轮送出的流量称为阻塞流。

阻塞流只要求把当前这些路径堵住，并不要求求出层次图自身的最大流。后者可能需要撤销本轮先前的选择，而撤销操作会经过反向边，离开当前允许的分层方向。

下一轮再对更新后的残量网络BFS。旧的最短路径全部被堵住，若还存在增广路，它的长度就会增加。层数最多到V−1V-1，因此最多进行O(V)O(V)轮分层。

从代码上看，就是两个 while。

内层把当前分层用完，外层负责重新分层。DFS一次只返回一条路的流量就够了，不必为了叫“阻塞流”而在一次递归里硬塞下所有路径。

当前弧为什么能一直往后走

如果每次进入 u都从第一条出边开始试，前面已经走不通的边会被检查很多遍。于是为每个点维护cur[u]，记录下一条需要尝试的边在 id[u]中的位置。

这里的 & 要保留。循环里修改i，也就修改了 cur[u]，下一次进入u 时才能接着往下找。

为什么已经失败的边可以跳过？看一次沿层次图的增广。正向残余容量减少，新增加的反向容量指向上一层，不能在本轮DFS中使用。因此，本轮可用的向前边只会减少，不会凭空增加。一个点的后续路径已经全部走不通，继续增广也不能让它重新通向汇点。

成功推流时，当前边可能还有容量，所以直接return pushed，让指针留在这条边上。只有它被用满，或者它后面再也到不了汇点，循环才继续往后走。

这个判断依赖固定的 level。下一轮 BFS 改了层数，所有cur 都要归零。

用 Dinic 求二分图最大匹配

设左部有nLn_L个点，右部有nRn_R个点。每条允许的配对连接左右两侧，要求每个点最多被选一次，并让配对数量最多。

先从“一对匹配”入手。让一单位流量经过一个左部点、一个右部点，再到汇点，它就可以代表选择这一对。

图中只画原边，建图时每条边仍要配上残量反边。所有原边容量都是1。

连边限制
s -> u左部点 u 最多参与一次匹配
u -> nL+v允许选择配对 (u,v)
nL+v -> t右部点 v 最多参与一次匹配

两侧在题目里都可能从 1 开始编号，所以右侧统一加上nL。取s=0、t=nL+nR+1，整个网络需要nL+nR+2 个点。

每个合法匹配都能变成相同大小的整数流。反过来，算法从零流开始，每次增广整数流量，容量为1 的配对边最终只会流过 0 或 1单位；源点和汇点一侧的容量又保证了每个点最多使用一次。这样，整数流也能还原成匹配，最大流量就是最大匹配数。

反向边在匹配里做了什么

只考虑三条允许的配对L1R1L_1R_1、L1R2L_1R_2、L2R1L_2R_1。如果先选了L1R1L_1R_1，下一轮可以找到残量路径

s→L2→R1→L1→R2→t.s\to L_2\to R_1\to L_1\to R_2\to t.

其中R1→L1R_1\to L_1是反向边。走过它会撤销原来的L1R1L_1R_1，随后改成L2R1L_2R_1和L1R2L_1R_2，匹配数从1 增加到 2。

这也解释了为什么不能看到某条配对边曾经流过，就立刻把它记成最终答案。要等最大流跑完，再检查残量。

完整代码

下面使用 C++17，保留 e + id 的邻接表写法。输入nL nR m，随后输入mm行 u v，表示允许左侧 u 与右侧 v配对。两侧编号分别属于 [1,nL] 和[1,nR]。输出第一行是最大匹配数，后面每行输出一对匹配。

配对边初始容量为 1，反边初始容量为0，所以最终 e[idx ^ 1].c == 1就表示选中了这条边。数组大小按 id.size()分配，左右两侧以及额外的源汇点都会被算进去；只按原题的 n+1分配，右侧点很容易越界。

上面的核心也能用于一般最大流，只需重新设置源汇并按原容量建图。容量须非负，总流量须能用ll 表示。深层图上的递归深度可能达到O(V)O(V)，数据规模很大时还要留意栈空间。

如果题目限制“经过点 u 的流量不能超过b”，可以把它拆成 u_in 和u_out，中间连一条容量为 b 的边。原来的入边接到u_in，出边从 u_out出发，经过这个点的流量就都受中间这条边限制。点容量也就转成了边容量。

复杂度与阈值匹配

一般网络中，一轮阻塞流最多增广O(E)O(E)次，每条路径长度为O(V)O(V)；当前弧把失败的边扫描控制在本轮O(E)O(E)次。加上最多O(V)O(V)轮分层，时间复杂度为O(V2E)O(V^2E)，空间为O(V+E)O(V+E)。

二分图匹配对应的标准单位网络可以进一步做到O(EV)O(E\sqrt V)，这里的EE包括源点和汇点的连边。这个界依赖匹配网络的结构，不能直接套给所有“边容量都是1”的网络。

之前那种给配对附上时间d、要求尽早完成全部匹配的题，也可以继续用这份建图。检查答案lim 时，只加入 d <= lim的配对边，再看最大流是否等于需要匹配的点数。可用边随 lim增大而增加，判定满足单调性，可以二分答案。

每次 check要重新建图，或者恢复初始残量容量。上一次检查留下的流量会影响下一次结果。

这里优化的是所有选中配对中最大的时间。若题目改成最小化总费用，目标就变了，下一篇再用费用流与带权匹配处理。

参考 MIT的 Blocking Flows 讲义。

entry.title: Dinic & Maximum Bipartite Matching
entry.content:
Read the original Chineseversion

In EK, each BFS findsone augmenting path. After pushing flow along it, we start searchingagain. The problem is that this BFS has already found the shortestdistances to many vertices, but we only use one path in the end. Thatfeels like a bit of a waste.

Could we keep the search results, find a few more augmenting paths ofthe same length, and only then run BFS again? Dinic takes this ideafurther.

First, divide theresidual network into levels

Let level[u] be the minimum number of residual edgesneeded to reach u from the source. BFS still only followsedges with positive residual capacity. Once we have the levels, we addone more condition to DFS.

In other words, each step must move to the next level. The graphformed by these edges is called the level graph.

When we reach the sink this way, the number of edges we have usedmust equal level[t], so we have found a shortest augmentingpath. Levels strictly increase along the path, which also means DFScannot go around a cycle. There is no need for the usualvis array.

What we divide into levels here is the current residualnetwork. Both original edges and reverse edges take part inBFS, as long as they have remaining capacity. If a reverse edge happensto go from levelkkto levelk+1k+1in this round, it can also belong to the level graph.

How much can we get out ofone BFS?

With the levels fixed, we repeatedly run DFS from the source. Eachtime we find a path, we push its bottleneck flow, until DFS returns0.

At this point, every source-to-sink path in the current level graphhas at least one saturated edge. We can no longer augment by movingthrough increasing levels. The flow sent in this round is called ablocking flow.

A blocking flow only needs to block these current paths. It does nothave to be a maximum flow of the level graph itself. Finding thatmaximum flow might require undoing earlier choices in this round, andundoing them would use reverse edges that go against the current leveldirection.

In the next round, we run BFS on the updated residual network. Allthe old shortest paths have been blocked, so if an augmenting path stillexists, it must be longer. The highest possible level isV−1V-1,which gives at mostO(V)O(V)rounds of building the level graph.

In code, this is just two while loops.

The inner loop uses up the current level graph, and the outer loopbuilds a new one. Each DFS only needs to return the flow along one path.There is no need to force all paths into a single recursive call justbecause we call the result a “blocking flow”.

Why canthe current-edge pointer keep moving forward?

If we start from the first outgoing edge every time we enteru, we will check the same unusable edges again and again.So we keep a cur[u] for each vertex, recording the positionin id[u] of the next edge to try.

The & matters here. Changing i insidethe loop also changes cur[u], so the next visit tou can continue from where we left off.

Why is it safe to skip an edge that has already failed? Consider oneaugmentation along the level graph. The forward residual capacitydecreases, and any newly added reverse capacity points to the previouslevel, so this round’s DFS cannot use it. The usable forward edges inthis round can therefore only disappear; no new ones become available.Once a vertex has no remaining path to the sink, further augmentationscannot make it reach the sink again.

After successfully pushing flow, the current edge may still havecapacity. We therefore use return pushed directly and leavethe pointer on this edge. The loop only moves on when the edge issaturated or there is no longer a path to the sink through it.

This reasoning depends on level staying fixed. When thenext BFS changes the levels, every cur must be reset tozero.

Using Dinic formaximum bipartite matching

Suppose there arenLn_Lvertices on the left andnRn_Rvertices on the right. Each allowed pair connects the two sides. We wantto choose as many pairs as possible, with each vertex chosen at mostonce.

Start with a single matched pair. If one unit of flow passes througha left vertex, then a right vertex, and finally reaches the sink, it canrepresent choosing that pair.

The diagram only shows original edges. When building the graph, eachedge still needs a reverse residual edge. Every original edge hascapacity 1.

EdgeConstraint
s -> uLeft vertex u can appear in at most one matchedpair
u -> nL+vThe pair (u,v) is allowed
nL+v -> tRight vertex v can appear in at most one matchedpair

Both sides may be numbered from 1 in the problem, so weadd nL to every right-side index. Set s=0 andt=nL+nR+1. The whole network then needsnL+nR+2 vertices.

Every valid matching can be turned into an integer flow of the samesize. In the other direction, the algorithm starts with zero flow andpushes an integer amount in each augmentation. A pairing edge withcapacity 1 will therefore carry either 0 or1 unit at the end. The capacities next to the source andsink also ensure that each vertex is used at most once. So an integerflow can be turned back into a matching, and the maximum flow valueequals the maximum matching size.

What do reverse edges doin a matching?

Consider just three allowed pairs:L1R1L_1R_1,L1R2L_1R_2,andL2R1L_2R_1.If we chooseL1R1L_1R_1first, we can find the following residual path in the next round:

s→L2→R1→L1→R2→t.s\to L_2\to R_1\to L_1\to R_2\to t.

Here,R1→L1R_1\to L_1is a reverse edge. Using it cancels the originalL1R1L_1R_1pair. We then replace it withL2R1L_2R_1andL1R2L_1R_2,increasing the matching size from 1 to 2.

This also explains why we cannot record a pairing edge as part of thefinal answer just because it has carried flow at some point. We need tofinish the maximum flow algorithm first, then check the residualcapacities.

Complete code

The following code uses C++17 and keeps the e + idadjacency-list structure. The input starts with nL nR m,followed bymmlines of u v, meaning that left vertex u canbe paired with right vertex v. The two sides are numberedwithin [1,nL] and [1,nR] respectively. Thefirst output line gives the maximum matching size, and each followingline gives one matched pair.

A pairing edge starts with capacity 1, and its reverseedge starts with capacity 0. So at the end,e[idx ^ 1].c == 1 means this edge has been selected. Thearrays are sized using id.size(), which includes both sidesand the extra source and sink. If we only allocate n+1entries based on the original problem, right-side vertices can easily goout of bounds.

The same core code also works for general maximum flow. We only needto set the source and sink again and build the graph with the givencapacities. Capacities must be non-negative, and the total flow must fitin ll. In a deep graph, the recursion depth can reachO(V)O(V),so keep an eye on stack space when the input is very large.

If a problem says “the flow through vertex u cannotexceed b”, we can split it into u_in andu_out, with an edge of capacity b betweenthem. Original incoming edges connect to u_in, and outgoingedges start from u_out. All flow through this vertex isthen limited by the edge in the middle. This turns a vertex capacityinto an edge capacity.

Complexity andmatching with a threshold

In a general network, finding a blocking flow takes at mostO(E)O(E)augmentations, and each path has lengthO(V)O(V).The current-edge pointers limit scans of failed edges toO(E)O(E)in each round. With at mostO(V)O(V)rounds of building the level graph, the time complexity isO(V2E)O(V^2E)and the space complexity isO(V+E)O(V+E).

For the standard unit network used in bipartite matching, the timebound improves toO(EV)O(E\sqrt V),whereEEincludes the edges connected to the source and sink. This bound dependson the structure of the matching network. We cannot apply it directly toevery network whose “edge capacities are all 1”.

For the kind of problem we discussed earlier, where each pair has atime d and we want to finish the whole matching as early aspossible, we can still use this construction. To check an answerlim, only add pairing edges with d <= lim,then see whether the maximum flow equals the number of vertices thatneed to be matched. As lim increases, more edges becomeavailable. The condition is monotonic, so we can binary-search theanswer.

For every check, rebuild the graph or restore theinitial residual capacities. Flow left over from the previous check willaffect the next result.

What we are minimising here is the largest time among all selectedpairs. If the problem changes to minimising total cost, the objective isdifferent. We will handle that in the next post on min-cost flow and weightedmatching.

Reference: MIT’snotes on Blocking Flows.

entry.title: 网络流初步 & 最大流
entry.content:
可以先把网络流想成在一张有向图上运送货物。货物从起点出发，沿着不同路线送到终点，每条路都有运输上限。最大流关心最多能送多少；如果每条路还要收运费，就会进一步遇到费用流。

网络流的基本概念

给定一张有向图，指定源点ss和汇点tt。每条边有容量c(u,v)c(u,v)，表示它最多能通过多少流量。我们希望从ss向tt送出尽量多的流量。

源点是流量的起点，汇点是流量的终点，其他点负责中转。比如只有s→a→ts\to a\to t这一条路径，两条边的容量分别为33和22，最终最多只能送出22。容量为33不意味着一定要送满，它只是这条边的上限。

一条边上实际通过的流量记为f(u,v)f(u,v)，必须满足

0≤f(u,v)≤c(u,v).0\le f(u,v)\le c(u,v).

中间点还要满足流量守恒。除了源点和汇点，每个点流进来的量等于流出去的量。不能凭空多出一部分，也不能把流量留在某个中间点。

如果把原图中的边记为ee，流量记为fef_e，那么对每个中间点vv，有

∑e:e 进入 vfe=∑e:e 离开 vfe.\sum_{e:\,e\text{ 进入 }v}f_e=\sum_{e:\,e\text{ 离开 }v}f_e.

总流量是源点的净流出量，也等于汇点的净流入量。可以同时使用多条路径；同一条边被几条路径使用时，它们经过这里的流量加起来仍然不能超过容量。

满足容量限制和流量守恒的一组流量分配，叫作可行流。流的大小通常记为|f||f|，计算时只统计源点的净流出量，不能把所有边上的流量直接相加。同一份货物经过几条边，不会因此变成几份。最大流就是在所有可行流中，让|f||f|最大。

再给每条边加上费用

如果走不同路线的代价不同，就给每条原边ee再加一个单位费用wew_e。这条边流过fef_e单位，就产生fewef_e w_e的费用，整个方案的总费用为

cost⁡(f)=∑e∈Efewe.\operatorname{cost}(f)=\sum_{e\in E}f_e w_e.

比如沿s→a→ts\to a\to t送货，两条边的单位费用分别为22和33，送一单位需要55，送两单位就需要1010。容量限制能送多少，费用则影响选择哪条路线。

这里要分清两个常见目标。固定流量的最小费用流要求恰好送出KK单位，在所有满足要求的方案中找费用最小的；如果最大流不足KK，就无解。最小费用最大流则先让流量最大，再在最大流方案中让费用最小，不能为了便宜而少送。

本文先处理最大流，从增广路和反向边入手。接着用 Dinic 与二分图最大匹配加快增广并处理配对问题，再在费用流与二分图带权匹配中加入费用。最后一篇最大流最小割、König 与 Dilworth背后的对偶会把这些问题的最优性联系起来。

从一条路径开始

先找一条从ss到tt的路径。如果沿途还能通过的量分别为5,3,75,3,7，这次最多只能送出33。路径上最小的剩余容量限制了整条路径，这个值通常叫瓶颈容量。

送完以后，再找下一条路径。问题就出在这次“再找”上。

反向边给了我们修改之前选择的机会

考虑四个点s,a,b,ts,a,b,t。原图有五条边s→as\to a、s→bs\to b、a→ba\to b、a→ta\to t、b→tb\to t，容量全部为11。

如果第一次选中了s→a→b→ts\to a\to b\to t，三条边都被用满。只看原图剩余容量，ss还可以到bb，但bb已经没法继续到tt，似乎只能得到11。

可直接选择s→a→ts\to a\to t和s→b→ts\to b\to t，明明能得到22。第一次的选择需要调整。

当a→ba\to b已经流过11时，我们额外允许沿b→ab\to a走11。走这条反向边，就把原来a→ba\to b上的流量减掉11。

这样又能找到一条路径

s→b→a→t.s\to b\to a\to t.

其中s→bs\to b和a→ta\to t各增加11，a→ba\to b减少11。最后留下的正好是那两条各送出11的路径，总流量变成22。沿着新的路径，每个中间点的流入与流出仍然平衡。

反向边记录的是此前流量可以撤销多少。 一条原边容量为cc、当前流量为ff，就对应两条残量边，正向剩余容量为c−fc-f，反向剩余容量为ff。只保留正残量的边，得到的图叫残量网络；其中从ss到tt的路径叫增广路。

代码只维护残余容量，每次送出 pushed 后写成

遍历到反向边时仍然用这两行。它会减少反向残量，同时把正向容量补回来，恰好完成撤销。

Ford-Fulkerson

Ford-Fulkerson的做法很直接。在残量网络里找到一条增广路，沿途推送瓶颈容量，再继续找，直到找不到为止。

用 DFS 就能实现找路。dfs(u, lim) 中的 lim表示当前路径最多还能送多少，到汇点就返回它。递归进入下一条边时传入min(lim, e[idx].c)，返回的正流量再用于更新残量。

这里有个容易写错的位置。某个儿子返回0，只说明这条分支失败，应该继续枚举其他出边。只有成功找到增广路时才提前返回；所有分支都试完后，函数最后才返回0。另外，每次重新找路前都要清空vis，上一次访问过的点这次可能仍然有用。

假设容量都是整数，最大流为FF。每次成功增广至少增加11，最多成功FF次。一次搜索为O(V+E)O(V+E)，包括最终失败的搜索，总上界为O((F+1)(V+E))O((F+1)(V+E))，常见写法是O(EF)O(EF)。这个界依赖流量的数值，容量很大时可能很慢。

无理数容量下，任意选路的 Ford-Fulkerson 甚至可能不终止。下面的 EK会规定选路方式，把复杂度限制在点数和边数上。

Edmonds-Karp

EK 每次用 BFS 找增广路。残余容量只决定一条边能不能走，BFS按边数分层，因此找到的是边数最少的路径。

例如一条路径有两条边，每条剩余容量都是11；另一条有三条边，每条都是100100。EK会先选择前者。这次增广能送出的量，等路径确定以后，再取路径上的最小残量。

BFS按队列顺序处理点，到某个点时，所有更少边数能到达的点都已先被发现。从边数为dd的点向外扩展，第一次发现的点就处在第d+1d+1层。这里没有按容量排序，也不需要优先队列。

保存路径和瓶颈

用 pre[v] 保存进入vv的那条边的编号，初始化为-1，同时作为未访问标记。源点要提前标记，否则残量反边可能把它重新加入队列。

为什么存边编号？同一对点之间可能有重边，只记前驱点不能确定究竟走了哪条边。知道边编号idx 后，前驱点就是 e[idx ^ 1].v。

flow[v] 保存本次 BFS 选出的源点到vv的路径瓶颈。扩展一条边时更新

到达汇点以后，flow[t] 就是这次增广量。这里的flow[v] 只服务于当前路径，不表示最终经过点vv的总流量。不用这个数组也可以，找到汇点后沿 pre回溯一次，重新取最小容量即可。

完整代码

继续使用 e + id 的邻接表。e保存所有边，id[u] 保存从uu出发的边编号；一次建边连续加入正向边和反向边，因此 idx ^ 1可以在它们之间切换。

输入 n m s t，接着输入mm行 u v c，点编号为[1,n]。要求源汇不同、容量为非负整数，容量及答案都能放进long long。

原图如果同时有u→vu\to v和v→uv\to u，分别调用两次add()，最终存下四条边。两条原边各有自己的残量反边，不能把它们混成一对。

EK 的时间复杂度为O(VE2)O(VE^2)，空间为O(V+E)O(V+E)。粗略看，BFS到各点的最短距离不会随增广而减小；同一条有向残量边被反复用满时，它的起点层数必须不断增加，所以一条边最多成为瓶颈O(V)O(V)次，总共只有O(VE)O(VE)次增广。再乘每次 BFS的开销，得到这个上界，通常省略孤立点初始化的影响。

没有增广路时，为什么就最大了

把所有点分成S,TS,T两部分，要求s∈Ss\in S、t∈Tt\in T，这就是一个源汇割。割的容量只统计原图中从SS指向TT的边

c(S,T)=∑u∈S,v∈Tc(u,v).c(S,T)=\sum_{u\in S,\,v\in T}c(u,v).

把SS内所有点的流量守恒式加起来，内部边会相互抵消，只剩跨越边界的净流量

|f|=f(S,T)−f(T,S)≤c(S,T).|f|=f(S,T)-f(T,S)\le c(S,T).

因此任意流都不会超过任意割的容量。反向跨割的流量要减掉，不能只统计从SS流出去的部分。

当算法找不到增广路时，令SS为残量网络中从ss还能到达的点，其他点属于TT。汇点到不了，自然在TT里。

原图中S→TS\to T的边全部满流，否则还能沿正向残量边走过去。原图中T→ST\to S的边流量全部为00，否则对应的反向残量边又能从SS走到TT。于是

|f|=c(S,T)−0=c(S,T).|f|=c(S,T)-0=c(S,T).

前面证明过任何流都被任何割限制住，现在两者相等，当前流就是最大流，这个割也就是最小割。最大流最小割定理把“已经找不到路了”变成了能验证的最优性证明。

EK 每轮 BFS 只增广一条路径。同一次 BFS得到的层次信息能不能再多用几次？接下来用 Dinic 与二分图最大匹配继续处理这个问题。

参考阅读 MIT6.046J Network Flow。

entry.title: Network Flow Basics & Maximum Flow
entry.content:
Read the original Chineseversion

We can start by thinking of network flow as moving goods through adirected graph. The goods travel from a starting point to a destinationalong different routes, and each road has a limit on how much it cancarry. Maximum flow asks how much we can send in total. If each roadalso charges a fee, we get to min-cost flow.

The basic ideas of networkflow

Given a directed graph, choose a sourcessand a sinktt.Each edge has a capacityc(u,v)c(u,v),which is the most flow it can carry. We want to send as much flow aspossible fromsstott.

The source is where flow starts, the sink is where it ends, and theother vertices pass it along. For example, suppose the only path iss→a→ts\to a\to t,with capacities33and22.We can send at most22units. A capacity of33does not mean we have to send33units; it is just the upper limit for that edge.

Write the actual flow through an edge asf(u,v)f(u,v).It must satisfy

0≤f(u,v)≤c(u,v).0\le f(u,v)\le c(u,v).

Intermediate vertices must also satisfy flow conservation. At everyvertex except the source and sink, the total incoming flow equals thetotal outgoing flow. Flow cannot appear out of nowhere, and we cannotleave some of it at an intermediate vertex.

If we write an original edge aseeand its flow asfef_e,then every intermediate vertexvvsatisfies

∑e:e enters vfe=∑e:e leaves vfe.\sum_{e:\,e\text{ enters }v}f_e=\sum_{e:\,e\text{ leaves }v}f_e.

The total flow is the net flow leaving the source, which also equalsthe net flow entering the sink. We can use several paths at once. Ifseveral paths share an edge, their combined flow through that edge muststill stay within its capacity.

A flow assignment that satisfies the capacity constraints and flowconservation is called a feasible flow. Its value isusually written as|f||f|.We only count the net flow leaving the source, rather than adding up theflow on every edge. The same goods do not become several batches justbecause they pass through several roads. A maximum flowis a feasible flow with the largest possible|f||f|.

Adding a cost to each edge

If different routes have different costs, give each original edgeeea cost per unitwew_e.Sendingfef_eunits through it costsfewef_e w_e,so the total cost is

cost⁡(f)=∑e∈Efewe.\operatorname{cost}(f)=\sum_{e\in E}f_e w_e.

For example, suppose the two edges ons→a→ts\to a\to tcost22and33per unit. Sending one unit costs55,and sending two costs1010.Capacity limits how much we can send, while cost affects which route wechoose.

There are two common goals to distinguish here. Min-cost flowwith a fixed value asks us to send exactlyKKunits and find the cheapest way to do so. If the maximum flow is lessthanKK,there is no solution. Min-cost maximum flow firstmaximises the flow, then minimises the cost among all maximum flows. Wecannot send less just to make it cheaper.

This post starts with maximum flow, using augmenting paths andreverse edges. Next, Dinic &Maximum Bipartite Matching speeds up augmentation and applies it topairing problems. Then Min-Cost Flow & WeightedBipartite Matching adds costs. The final post, The Duality Behind Max-Flow Min-Cut,König and Dilworth, connects the reasons why these solutions areoptimal.

Starting with one path

First, find a path fromsstott.If the remaining capacities along it are5,3,75,3,7,we can send at most33units this time. The smallest remaining capacity limits the whole path.This is usually called the bottleneck capacity.

After sending that flow, we look for another path. This is wherethings get interesting.

Reverse edges letus change earlier choices

Consider four verticess,a,b,ts,a,b,t.The original graph has five edges:s→as\to a,s→bs\to b,a→ba\to b,a→ta\to t,andb→tb\to t.Every edge has capacity11.

Suppose we first chooses→a→b→ts\to a\to b\to t.All three edges become full. If we only look at the remaining capacitiesof the original edges,sscan still reachbb,butbbcan no longer reachtt.It looks as if we can only send11unit.

But choosings→a→ts\to a\to tands→b→ts\to b\to tclearly gives us22.We need a way to adjust our first choice.

Once11unit has flowed througha→ba\to b,we also allow11unit to travel alongb→ab\to a.Using this reverse edge removes11unit of the earlier flow ona→ba\to b.

We can now find another path:

s→b→a→t.s\to b\to a\to t.

We add11unit to boths→bs\to banda→ta\to t,and remove11unit froma→ba\to b.What remains is exactly the two paths carrying11unit each, giving a total flow of22.Flow conservation still holds at every intermediate vertex along the newpath.

A reverse edge records how much of an earlier flow we canundo. An original edge with capacityccand current flowffhas two residual edges: a forward edge with remaining capacityc−fc-f,and a reverse edge with remaining capacityff.Keeping only edges with positive residual capacity gives us the residualnetwork. Anss-to-ttpath in this network is called an augmenting path.

The code only stores residual capacities. After sendingpushed units, we update them with

We use the same two lines when traversing a reverse edge. They reduceits residual capacity and restore capacity on the forward edge, which isexactly how we undo earlier flow.

Ford-Fulkerson

Ford-Fulkerson is quite straightforward. Find an augmenting path inthe residual network, send its bottleneck capacity along it, and keeplooking until no such path remains.

We can use DFS to find a path. In dfs(u, lim),lim is the most flow the current path can still carry.Return it when we reach the sink. When moving to the next edge, passmin(lim, e[idx].c), then use any positive flow returned toupdate the residual capacities.

There is an easy mistake to make here. If one recursive call returns0, only that branch has failed; we should keep trying theother outgoing edges. Return early only after finding an augmentingpath. If every branch fails, return 0 at the end of thefunction. Also, clear vis before every new search. A vertexvisited last time may still be useful this time.

Assume all capacities are integers and the maximum flow isFF.Every successful augmentation adds at least11,so there are at mostFFsuccessful augmentations. Each search takesO(V+E)O(V+E).Including the final failed search, the total upper bound isO((F+1)(V+E))O((F+1)(V+E)),often written asO(EF)O(EF).This bound depends on the numerical value of the flow, so it can be slowwhen capacities are large.

With irrational capacities, Ford-Fulkerson may not even terminate ifpaths are chosen arbitrarily. Edmonds-Karp specifies how to choosepaths, giving a complexity bound in terms of the numbers of vertices andedges.

Edmonds-Karp

Edmonds-Karp, or EK, uses BFS to find each augmenting path. Residualcapacity only decides whether an edge can be used. BFS buildslayers by the number of edges, so it finds a path with thefewest edges.

For example, one path has two edges, each with remaining capacity11.Another has three edges, each with remaining capacity100100.EK chooses the first one. Once the path is fixed, we take its smallestresidual capacity to decide how much flow to send.

BFS processes vertices in queue order. When a vertex is reached, allvertices reachable using fewer edges have already been discovered.Expanding from a vertex at distancedd,any newly discovered vertex belongs to layerd+1d+1.We are not sorting by capacity, and we do not need a priority queue.

Recording the path andits bottleneck

Use pre[v] to store the index of the edge enteringvv.Initialise it to -1, which also marks the vertex asunvisited. Mark the source in advance, or a residual reverse edge mightput it back in the queue.

Why store an edge index? There may be parallel edges between the sametwo vertices, so the previous vertex alone cannot tell us which edge weused. Given an edge index idx, its starting vertex ise[idx ^ 1].v.

flow[v] stores the bottleneck of thesource-to-vvpath chosen by this BFS. When extending the path along an edge, updateit with

Once we reach the sink, flow[t] is the amount we cansend in this augmentation. Here, flow[v] only describes thecurrent path. It does not represent the total flow throughvvin the final solution. We can also leave out this array and walk backalong pre after reaching the sink to find the smallestcapacity.

Full code

We keep using the e + id adjacency list. estores all edges, and id[u] stores the indices of the edgesleavinguu.Each call to add an edge inserts its forward and reverse edgesconsecutively, so idx ^ 1 switches between them.

The input starts with n m s t, followed bymmlines of u v c. Vertices are numbered [1,n].The source and sink must be different, capacities must be non-negativeintegers, and both the capacities and the answer must fit inlong long.

If the original graph contains bothu→vu\to vandv→uv\to u,call add() separately for each one. This stores four edgesin total. Each original edge has its own residual reverse edge; the twooriginal edges must not be treated as one pair.

EK takesO(VE2)O(VE^2)time andO(V+E)O(V+E)space. Roughly speaking, the shortest BFS distance to each vertex neverdecreases as we augment. Before the same directed residual edge canbecome full again, the layer of its starting vertex must increase. Anedge can therefore be a bottleneck at mostO(V)O(V)times, givingO(VE)O(VE)augmentations in total. Multiplying by the cost of each BFS gives thisbound, usually ignoring the cost of initialising isolated vertices.

Why isthe flow maximum when no augmenting path remains?

Split all vertices into two setsS,TS,T,withs∈Ss\in Sandt∈Tt\in T.This is anss-ttcut. Its capacity only counts original edges directed fromSStoTT:

c(S,T)=∑u∈S,v∈Tc(u,v).c(S,T)=\sum_{u\in S,\,v\in T}c(u,v).

Adding up the flow-balance equations over the vertices inSS,the internal edges cancel, leaving only the net flow across theboundary:

|f|=f(S,T)−f(T,S)≤c(S,T).|f|=f(S,T)-f(T,S)\le c(S,T).

So any flow is bounded by the capacity of any cut. We must subtractthe flow crossing back fromTTtoSS,rather than just counting what leavesSS.

When no augmenting path remains, letSSbe the vertices still reachable fromssin the residual network, and put all other vertices inTT.The sink is unreachable, so it belongs toTT.

Every original edge fromSStoTTis full; otherwise, we could reach further along its forward residualedge. Every original edge fromTTtoSScarries zero flow; otherwise, its reverse residual edge would let usmove fromSStoTT.Therefore,

|f|=c(S,T)−0=c(S,T).|f|=c(S,T)-0=c(S,T).

We already showed that every flow is bounded by every cut. Now theirvalues are equal, so the current flow is a maximum flow and this cut isa minimum cut. The max-flow min-cut theorem turns “we cannot findanother path” into a proof of optimality that we can actually check.

EK augments along just one path per BFS. Could we reuse the layersfound by the same BFS a few more times? We will pick this up in Dinic & Maximum BipartiteMatching.
